stem.en: Kabir shuffles a pack of cards and deals himself a hand. Every card is a spade, in order. He says "that was impossible". Was it?

text.en: No. That exact hand is exactly as likely as any other exact hand. What is unlikely is "a hand that looks special", because there are very few special-looking hands among the enormous number of ordinary-looking ones.

feedback.en: Any single hand can happen. The one he got has the same chance as the boring one he usually gets.

text.en: It was more likely than an ordinary hand, because the pack was new.

feedback.en: If the pack was truly shuffled, the order is gone. If not, it was not a shuffle.

text.en: It shows the shuffle was rigged.

feedback.en: Possibly. But a fair shuffle produces this hand once in every 300,000 or so tries, which is rare, not impossible.

explanation.en: Every exact arrangement is equally likely. "Special" outcomes are rare because there are few of them, not because any of them is disfavoured. That is entropy: a count of arrangements that look the same.
